inspection_summary: Inspected all 777 normalized lines. The source develops a Fourier-weighted pair statistic for zeta-zero differences under RH, proves its low-frequency asymptotic by matching two mean-square evaluations of an explicit-formula identity, derives simple-zero and gap consequences through chosen kernels, and isolates off-diagonal prime correlations as the obstruction beyond the proved frequency range. The conjectural extension is compared with unitary random-matrix statistics and propagated to higher correlations and extreme-gap predictions. Prose is coherent, but several displayed formulas are partially or wholly lost in extraction; units retain only recoverable claims and flag exact-formula dependence for scan verification.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and statement of the Fourier statistic theorem
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the weighted pair transform F and states its RH-conditional symmetry, positivity lower bound, and asymptotic below unit frequency.

sections_inspected.label: Kernel consequences and spacing corollaries
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Explains Fourier-kernel transfer from F to zero-difference sums, states simple-zero and normalized-gap consequences, and motivates the gap threshold through a related Dedekind-zeta application.

sections_inspected.label: Large-frequency conjecture and spectral analogies
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Diagnoses failure of naive extrapolation, proposes the pair-correlation law, compares matrix symmetry classes, extends the analogy to higher correlations and gaps, and cautions about slow numerical convergence.

sections_inspected.label: Explicit formula
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Builds the zero-to-prime bridge used in the proof by subtracting shifted logarithmic-derivative formulas under RH.

sections_inspected.label: Proof of the theorem
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Evaluates the zero side and prime side as matched mean squares, proves the stated range by scale-dependent dominance, and identifies shifted-prime correlations and a character-sum analogue beyond that range.

sections_inspected.label: Proofs of the corollaries
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Selects Fourier kernels to extract weighted statistics, bounds the multiplicity moment to obtain simple zeros, and uses a triangular kernel to force subaverage gaps.

sections_inspected.label: References and affiliation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Non-substantive bibliography and closing matter; inspected for complete coverage.

accepted_units.title: A dilation inequality rules out uniform continuation of the low-frequency law
accepted_units.why_material: Assuming the small-alpha formula across a large interval makes two scaled kernel consequences incompatible: the observable satisfies one dilation inequality while its predicted main term satisfies the opposite growth pattern. This forces a behavioral transition near alpha equal to one.
accepted_units.context_note: Preserves the contradiction and the resulting expectation that large-alpha averages approach one.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: the OCR of inequality symbols is imperfect, but the two compared dilation relations and conclusion are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.why_material: Continuing the unitary analogy leads to a calculable nearest-neighbor distribution and the qualitative predictions that normalized consecutive gaps have liminf zero and unbounded limsup, showing the proved gap result is far from the expected truth.

accepted_units.why_material: The author notes that available zero computations could generate the relevant statistics but warns, using Gram-law failures, that finite-height evidence may poorly reflect the conjectured asymptotic regime.

accepted_units.title: Subtracting shifted explicit formulas links a smoothed zero sum to prime sums
accepted_units.why_material: The proof constructs its central zero-to-prime identity by writing a logarithmic-derivative explicit formula at two reflected shifts, subtracting them under RH, and estimating the remaining functional-equation and trivial-zero terms.
accepted_units.context_note: The exact lemma display is missing, so this unit records only the method-level bridge explicitly supported by the surrounding prose and surviving terms.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Critical: equation (18), the lemma's main display, is absent and several later displays are fragmented. Scan verification is mandatory before using the exact identity, coefficients, or error term.

accepted_units.title: A mean square localizes the zero sum and recovers the pair transform
accepted_units.why_material: Squaring and integrating the zero side creates a double-zero sum; tails outside the target height range are controlled by local zero counts, and a residue integral produces the weight w, identifying the result with F after x=T^alpha. Nonnegativity then supplies the theorem's lower bound.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the L=R setup, boundary exclusion, residue evaluation, normalization, and positivity conclusion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: displays (23)-(26) are fragmented but their transformations are narrated. Exact constants and kernels require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Quantitative Parseval handles an infinite Dirichlet-series mean square
accepted_units.why_material: The prime side is evaluated with a quantitative Parseval identity whose coefficient-dependent error permits the infinite Dirichlet series; the author contrasts it with a weaker polynomial-only mean-square theorem and explains the methodological choice.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the initial elementary term and both Parseval alternatives.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: equations (27) and (28) are visually damaged; the prose comparison is reliable, while the exact formulas need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Three x-ranges isolate the dominant term and prove the low-frequency asymptotic
accepted_units.why_material: Prime-number-theorem estimates, error-term mean squares, and Cauchy-Schwarz are organized into three x regimes. Their dominant terms combine with the zero-side identity after x=T^alpha to yield the theorem uniformly below alpha=1.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains the mean-square calculation, the stated error controls, the three-case phase split, and final matching step.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: several displays are incomplete and exponent typography is unreliable; the regime boundaries and proof architecture are readable, but exact estimates require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Beyond unit frequency, off-diagonal shifted-prime correlations become main-order
accepted_units.why_material: For x>T, prior errors cease to be negligible and termwise integration leaves too many nondiagonal contributions. Regrouping exposes shifted von Mangoldt correlations; their conjectured mean gives the desired order for 1<=alpha<2, while additional independence of errors would extend the prediction through all larger alpha.
accepted_units.context_note: This identifies both the precise proof bottleneck and the layered conjectural assumptions proposed to overcome it.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: equation (32) is badly fragmented and equation (33) is only partly clean; the prose-supported off-diagonal mechanism is recoverable, but exact weights require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: A character-average analogue supports stability past the proved boundary
accepted_units.why_material: A q-analogue replaces the continuous mean square by an average over characters and is shown in progressively wider parameter ranges, providing independent structural evidence that no new large-alpha transition is expected even though sharper error analysis is needed.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the analogue, unconditional established range, GRH-conditional wider range, parameter correspondence, and stated limitation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: equation (34) and range symbols are OCR-damaged; qualitative comparison and conditional range expansion are readable, but exact exponents require scan verification.

accepted_units.why_material: The proof of Corollary 1 explicitly chooses sinc and squared-sinc kernels and computes their transform-weighted integrals against F, exemplifying targeted observable design under a bandlimit.
accepted_units.context_note: Connects the abstract convolution bridge to the two concrete corollary kernels.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: transformed-kernel symbols and integrals are degraded; the chosen sinc profiles are visible, but constants need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: The diagonal pair mass controls the second moment of zero multiplicities
accepted_units.why_material: Counting zeros with multiplicity identifies equal-ordinate pairs with the multiplicity second moment. Bounding that diagonal contribution by the nonnegative kernel sum and comparing it with the total zero count yields the stated positive proportion of simple zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the multiplicity convention, diagonal identity, kernel domination, asymptotic bound, and conversion to a simple-zero count.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: several summation displays and the final constant are OCR-fragmented; the counting mechanism is clear, but exact constants require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: A triangular Fourier kernel forces gaps below the mean
accepted_units.why_material: A compactly supported triangular transform gives a computable lower bound for close pairs. After removing diagonal terms, positivity of C(A) for some A<1 guarantees a subaverage normalized gap; evaluating at 0.68 supplies the explicit stated constant and exposes kernel optimization as the route to improvement.
accepted_units.context_note: Keeps the kernel choice, lower-bound calculation, treatment of diagonal terms, positivity argument, and nonoptimality caveat together.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the transform notation and close-pair display are fragmented, though C(A), its positivity mechanism, and the value 0.68 are readable; scan-check exact normalization.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: From a transform theorem to local zero statistics

within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The extraction damages several exact transforms and constants, and the proved information remains restricted below unit frequency.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Matched mean squares as a zero-to-prime proof architecture
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The theorem is obtained by placing zeros and primes on opposite sides of an explicit-formula identity, evaluating the square mean of each representation, and matching their asymptotics after x=T^alpha.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The central explicit-formula display is missing from the extraction, so the architecture is supported but formula-level synthesis requires scan verification.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: The unit-frequency boundary is an arithmetic off-diagonal boundary
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The transition at alpha near one is simultaneously visible as failure of the low-frequency output law, loss of diagonal dominance in the proof, and emergence of shifted-prime correlations; the character analogue suggests the conjectured stable regime without proving it.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The shifted-prime approximations and independence assumptions are explicitly conjectural, and the q-analogue has restricted or conditional ranges.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Pair statistics select a spectral model and generate higher-order predictions
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The completed pair law favors unitary rather than orthogonal or symplectic statistics, and that model choice propagates to determinantal k-tuple correlations and extreme consecutive-gap predictions.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Only the low-frequency pair transform is proved here; the completion, higher correlations, and extreme-gap claims remain conjectural analogical consequences.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Positive kernels turn aggregate pair mass into arithmetic existence statements
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Nonnegative kernels let aggregate pair-correlation estimates dominate diagonal multiplicity mass or count sufficiently close off-diagonal pairs, yielding respectively many simple zeros and the existence of subaverage gaps.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The numerical constants depend on nonoptimal kernels and are not claimed to be sharp.
